    "languages": ["fr", "de", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5

    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },

    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },

    "languages": ["en", "grc"],

    "confidence": 0.3

    "chain": "Wem + bley; wem (Old English) = blemish, also 'wem' in Scots = to go astray; bley = pale, also 'blea' = bare",
    "reading": "A bare straying — the blemish of wandering, a place where one loses the path and finds the wild",
    "languages": ["en", "sco", "ang"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },

    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Wembley ~ Hebrew 'v'em' (and mother) + 'ley' (to me) ~ Arabic 'wam' (to be heavy) + 'bali' (my mind)",

    "languages": ["he", "ar", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Wembley possibly from 'Wemba' (Old English personal name) + 'leah' — but 'wemb' also means womb in Old English",
    "reading": "Womb‑clearing — a birthing grove, a place where the hidden is brought forth from the maternal dark",

    "confidence": 0.5

    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3

    "languages": ["en", "enm"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  }
]
